title: Plural of short newer -i words: -eja/-ejä
summary: For these short newer -i words, replace -i with -eja/-ejä: bussi (“bus”) → busseja.
objectives: Form the plural partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.

These short i-retaining word types keep i in the singular partitive but replace final -i with -eja/-ejä in the plural partitive. Keep strong consonants. Vowel harmony is the choice of a or ä from the word’s vowels: a, o or u select -eja; only e/i or front vowels select -ejä. Older -i words and longer words have other patterns.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: Replace final -i with -eja; keep ss: bussi → busseja.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “bus”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Replace final -i with -eja; keep strong pp: kuppi → kuppeja.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “cup”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Replace final -i with -eja; keep strong kk: pankki → pankkeja.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “bank”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Replace final -i with -eja; keep ss: passi → passeja.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “passport”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “post”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “taxi”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.

examples.english: wine · -i → -ejä; only neutral vowels select ä
steps: Replace final -i with -ejä; only neutral vowels select ä: viini → viinejä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “wine”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Replace final -i with -ejä; y selects ä: tyyli → tyylejä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “style”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Do not assume every -i word belongs to this family.
Keep strong kk and pp in pankkeja and kuppeja.
Neutral e/i select -ejä when there is no back vowel.
